definitions.explanation: A soldier or guard stationed to keep watch over a place, standing guard at an entrance, gate, or post to detect intruders.

examples.japanese: {門|もん}の{前|まえ}に{番兵|ばんぺい}が{立|た}っている。
examples.english: A sentry is standing in front of the gate.

examples.japanese: {番兵|ばんぺい}が{夜通|よどお}し{見張|みは}りをする。
examples.english: The sentry keeps watch all night long.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{番兵|ばんぺい}は{不審|ふしん}な{人物|じんぶつ}を{見|み}つけて{呼|よ}び{止|と}めた。
examples.english: The castle sentry spotted a suspicious person and called out to stop them.

notes:
Composed of {番|ばん} (watch, guard duty) + {兵|へい} (soldier). Refers to a soldier posted to stand guard; common in historical and military contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {番兵|ばんぺい}を{置|お}く: to post a sentry
- {番兵|ばんぺい}に{立|た}つ: to stand guard
- {番兵|ばんぺい}の{交代|こうたい}: changing of the guard

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歩哨|ほしょう}: sentinel — more technical, formal military term
- {見張|みは}り: lookout — general watching, not necessarily a soldier
